title: Can ChatGPT Serve as a Supportive Tool for Multidisciplinary Tumor Boards? A Single-Center, Retrospective Analysis
summary:
This study compares historical decisions made by tumor boards (expert groups that collectively decide on cancer treatments) with recommendations generated by Artificial Intelligence (AI) in the form of large language models (LLMs). We examine how accurately these AI systems can replicate the decisions of experienced medical teams and whether their accuracy can be improved through various optimization methods.
The study analyzes anonymized data from patients with colorectal cancer, liver tumors, and soft tissue sarcomas discussed in tumor boards at our hospital over the past five years. We test three versions of the AI systems: (1) base models without adaptation, (2) models with access to current medical guidelines, and (3) models specifically trained on oncological data.
The goal is to assess whether these AI technologies could serve as support tools for physicians in the future, especially in hospitals with fewer specialized experts. The study could help improve the quality of cancer treatment and make medical expertise more widely available.
conditions: Malignant neoplasm of other connective and soft tissue
Malignant neoplasm of liver and intrahepatic bile ducts

interventions.name: Historical Tumor Board Decisions: This arm contains the actual historical decisions made by multidisciplinary tumor boards for oncological patients, based on the existing anonymized clinical dataset (including colorectal carcinomas, esophageal carcinoma, gastric carcinoma, pancreatic carcinoma, mali
Base LLM Recommendations: This arm contains treatment recommendations generated by large language models (LLMs) without additional optimization when applied to the same anonymized patient data.

RAG-enhanced LLM Recommendations: This arm contains treatment recommendations generated by LLMs enhanced with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), which incorporates current medical guidelines into the models' responses.

Fine-tuned LLM Recommendations: This arm contains treatment recommendations generated by LLMs that have undergone specific fine-tuning on the anonymized clinical dataset of historical tumor board cases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Patients with confirmed diagnoses of cancers.
- Cases with comprehensive documentation of tumor board decisions and clinical data.
Exclusion criteria:
- Cases lacking comprehensive documentation of tumor board decisions or missing significant clinical data.
- Patients whose cases were discussed in emergency settings outside regular tumor board meetings.
